invariants.name: A write outside the scratch class gets the write checks
Each commit message gets the STE check of the commit surface
Each merge has a profile grant or a covering prompt of a person

abstraction.hides: The fold of the earlier steps of a command over one body file, the and-or links and the nesting of each parsed command, the names of the reader steps, and the slug form of a repo name.
callersKnow: stagedText gives text, unread with the disk text, or missing. A caller judges text, judges the disk text of an unread body, and skips a missing body.
stagedReader is the one disk read at the hook edge. ghBody and commitMessage take it as a parameter.
The STE hook adds one note and one unread-body event for each unread body. The other 3 body hooks keep the disk check with no note.
judge adds the chain line only to a deny of a shell event with 2 or more top-level commands, after combineAll.
foreignRepo gives the named repo only when no origin exists or sameRepo is false.
abstraction.deletionTest: Without stagedText, each of the 4 body hooks must parse the steps before its body step, or keep the disk read that misses a body that the same command writes. Without chainSteps, the chain line needs a second parse in dispatch.ts.

alternatives.name: The disk read of each body hook
alternatives.rejectedBecause: A body that the same command writes passes with the old text.

alternatives.name: Each write as certain
alternatives.rejectedBecause: A write after || or inside if can skip, so the hook judges text that the command does not send.

alternatives.name: A skip of an unread body
alternatives.rejectedBecause: 8 denies of the hook before this change become an allow.

alternatives.name: The shellSteps count for the chain line
alternatives.rejectedBecause: It drops cd, so the line names fewer steps than the command holds.

omitted: The model takes the commit message as a true observation, so it has no staged body, no unread body and no note.
The chain line changes no verdict kind, so no action of the model stands for it. The chain-deny-line controls examine it.
The PR body, ticket and duplicate PR hooks are unmodelled in the registry. Their controls examine the staged read and the origin rule.
skill-path, the email note, the template kind and the PR length note decide no guard verdict. Their controls examine them.

bounds: Attended and unattended sessions, four base authorities, three working-tree authorities, two PRs, two channels, a guard error or none, and prompts of one or two of seven clause classes from four sources.
Each combination of four path facts for one write and an optional commit.
Each set of changes from four change kinds in three places, and 16 git commands with their documented effects.
One repo at the path that the session makes, one record of that path, its settle window, and a repo of another process that appears after the window.
A HEAD whose gates pass or fail under the base profile or an edited profile, one gate run, and one push or commit with or without a hook skip to three targets.

negative.defect: The destructive guard passes a hook-skip push whose gate record holds another profile blob than the source and its merge base, so a push under an edited profile skips the git hooks.

limits: The hook reads the command text at PreToolUse and never sees the result of a step.
A redirect on a compound command, such as done > body.md, is no step, so the hook reads the disk.
A write in a nested shell, a substitution or a function gives an unread body, also when it always runs.
A deny masks the unread note, as ADR 0022 says for each advice finding.
The finite model takes the commit message and the prompt source as true observations.
Exact-head CI, review, Shipping and every ordinary gate stay required.
